Counterexample at the mechanism level. Step 78, action 3, refuted every program of a committee of 2. Rows where every program was wrong; this is the mechanic to repair:
  - row `block | ACTION3 | [player,portal]`, object token_0: observed x 33 -> 18; predicted x 33 -> 3 (1 program); x 33 -> 0 (1 program)
Rows where every program was right on this transition; keep these mechanics as the earlier programs had them:
  - player | ACTION3 | [block,block,portal]: no_change
  - block | ACTION3 | [player,portal]: no_change
  - block | ACTION3 | [portal]: no_change
  - target | ACTION3 | [portal]: no_change

  - target | ACTION3 | [portal]: no_change
  - target | ACTION3 | [portal]: no_change
  - portal | ACTION3 | [block,block,block,player,target,target,target,target]: no_change

Repair hypothesis for this seed: the rule for the row(s) above is decided by a bound of the playable area that the frame does not draw. Write that rule first and verify it on the counterexample and on every earlier transition. Keep every other mechanic as the earlier programs had it; do not key the rule to this step.

Rule for this repair: a movement stops because of a visible object, a field of an object, or a bound that a visible object marks. Do not infer invisible floors, corridors or regions from where objects stopped; a repair that adds coordinate constants the earlier programs did not need is a lookup table and will be rejected.
